headline: U.S. Approves First mRNA Vaccine for Flu
meta_description: The U.S. has approved Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine, marking a breakthrough in immunization technology and offering a new tool against seasonal illness.
summary_short: Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine has received U.S. approval, becoming the first vaccine of its kind to protect against influenza using messenger RNA technology.
body:
The U.S. has approved Moderna's mRNA vaccine for influenza—a historic first that brings cutting-edge vaccine technology to the fight against seasonal flu.

This approval marks a significant milestone in immunization. After the success of mRNA vaccines against COVID-19, researchers have now successfully adapted the same platform to target influenza. The development expands the toolkit available to public health officials and opens new possibilities for how we prevent respiratory illness.

The breakthrough demonstrates that mRNA technology extends beyond pandemic response. With flu season recurring annually and affecting millions, an effective new vaccine option could help reduce hospitalizations and deaths. This approval reflects years of scientific progress and offers hope for stronger flu protection in coming seasons.
quick_facts: Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine is the first of its kind approved in the U.S.
The vaccine uses messenger RNA technology, same platform as COVID vaccines
Approval expands mRNA vaccine applications beyond pandemic response
